title: Every Summer Has a Sunday Night
prompt:
[Intro: strummed acoustic guitar, a sigh, crickets]

[Verse 1: raspy male voice, quiet]
Towels on the railing, fire's burning low
The kids are getting quiet, 'cause they know
The cooler's by the door, the bags are by the stair
You're looking at the water like it's already not there

[Chorus: second voice in harmony, band enters softly]
Every summer has a Sunday night
Every party has a kitchen light
Every kid has got a driveway and a wave goodbye
Every summer has a Sunday night

[Verse 2: voice warmer, bass and brushes]
I used to fight it, used to sulk the whole way home
Used to waste the last day wishing it would slow
My father did the same, he'd go quiet by noon
Took me forty years to hear a different tune

[Chorus: fuller, electric guitar answering]
Every summer has a Sunday night
Every party has a kitchen light
Every kid has got a driveway and a wave goodbye
Every summer has a Sunday night

[Guitar Solo: slow, bluesy, electric]

[Bridge: acoustic and voice, almost spoken]
That's not the sad part. That's the frame.
You don't hang a picture without one.

[Verse 3: quiet, to her]
So come sit down. There's an hour left of gold.
I'm not gonna spend it getting old.

[Final Chorus: full band, crowd of family voices]
Every summer has a Sunday night
Every party has a kitchen light
Every kid has got a driveway and a wave goodbye
Every summer has a Sunday night
And tonight's a good one

[Outro: acoustic guitar, a screen door, a loon on the lake]
style: Late-1980s acoustic rock power ballad with a country ache, raspy slightly nasal male rock singer singing quietly, second voice in close harmony on the choruses, a family of voices on the last chorus, nearly spoken bridge, 70 BPM, G major, slow easy feel, strummed and picked acoustic guitars, bass, drums with brushes then light sticks, clean bluesy sustained electric guitar solo, a little pedal steel, warm dry simple mix, wistful, accepting, tender
